text: Introduction
trace: Introduction

text: This document specifies O-Cloud Interoperability testing \(IOT\) in accordance with O-RAN specified interfaces as defined in,\[3\],\[4\], \[9\],\[10\] and \[11\] which includes O-Cloud Notification API, AAL and O2.
trace: Introduction
Introduction
Introduction
Introduction
Introduction

text: 1 Scope
trace: 1 Scope

text: The present document specifies IOT testing for O-Cloud and peer device\(s\) or system\(s\) from different vendors connected by O-Cloud Interfaces/APIs. This document will specify the SUTs, testing methodology and the IOT test cases over O-Cloud Notification API, AAL O2 IMS and DMS interface.

text: 4 Testing methodology
trace: 2 References --> 4 Testing methodology

text: 4.1 System under test
trace: 2 References --> 4.1 System under test

text: Interoperability testing is performed to validate the end-to-end functionality between the O-Cloud and peer devices or systems from different vendors connected by interfaces as defined in,\[3\],\[4\],\[9\],\[10\] and \[11\]. This document primarily focuses on scenarios where the System Under Test \(SUT\) for interoperability testing is comprised of different Device Under Test \(DUTs\) and its interconnecting IOT interface. SUT for O-Cloud IOT refers to the O-Cloud platform, peer devices, and interfaces provided by O-Cloud, as illustrated in Figure 5.1-1 of O-RAN WG1 O-RAN Architecture Description, Clause 5.1\[1\] and Architecture Diagram in Figure 4.2-1 of O-RAN WG6 AAL GAnP, Clause 4.2 \[5\]
trace: 2 References --> 4.1 System under test

text: O-Cloud provides following APIs and Interfaces:
trace: 2 References --> 4.1 System under test

  * O2dms interface as described in O-RAN.WG6.O2DMS-INTERFACE-K8S-PROFILE \[10\] for NF Deployments.
  * O-Cloud Notification API, as described in O-RAN.WG6.O-Cloud Notification API.\[1\].
  * AAL interface, as described in O-RAN.WG6.AAL-Common-API \[4\].

text: 4.2 Test method
trace: 2 References --> 4.2 Test method

text: 4.2.1 Objective
trace: 2 References --> 4.2 Test method --> 4.2.1 Objective

text: O-Cloud IOT test focus on verifying the functional correctness between device peers. Performance test and security test are not in the scope.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2 Test method --> 4.2.1 Objective

text: To validate the functionality of production grade DUTs, it is important that the DUTs are not negatively impacted with the utilization of internal functions, so the Device in production environment should not be used for test.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2 Test method --> 4.2.1 Objective

text: The DUTs are used as black boxes for positive testing, negative testing, abnormal testing, etc.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2 Test method --> 4.2.1 Objective

text: 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up

text: Interoperability tests are performed with a set of testing tools which are used to both apply active stimulus and as well as monitoring and measurements of the DUTs. Non-DUT devices or corresponding emulation tools can be used as active stimulus during the test. Passive monitoring and measurement tools can be used to watch the status of DUTs, collect the information exchanges, and capture the logs during the test.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up

text: There is no constrain on the number of DUTs, but there shall be at least one for each DUT. DUTs shall be connected by corresponding interface before the test.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up

text: For each test is differ from others, the suggested tools and the set-up are be detailed in the corresponding configuration section of each test.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up
2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up
2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up
2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up

text: 4.2.3 Testing procedure
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.3 Testing procedure

text: In adherence to the specifications, the System Under Test \(SUT\) and the test tool are meticulously configured and connected to the device, strictly following the predefined conditions for each test case.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.3 Testing procedure

text: The test steps outlined in the test case are executed sequentially.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.3 Testing procedure

text: The tester is responsible for diligently documenting crucial test information during and after the testing process, enabling detailed comparisons and analyses against the expected outcomes.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.3 Testing procedure

text: It is crucial to note that each test case remains independent of one another.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.3 Testing procedure

text: 4.2.4 Statistics and analysis of key indicators
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.4 Statistics and analysis of key indicators

text: The test execution adheres to the predefined conditions and procedures specified in the test case.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.4 Statistics and analysis of key indicators

text: During the testing process, the tester may capture and record test result, including success or failure, along with corresponding metric data, such as throughput, latency, and device volume.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.4 Statistics and analysis of key indicators

text: The expected test results serve as the benchmark for evaluating the test success. If the actual test results align with the expected outcomes, the test is considered successful.
trace: 2 References --> 4.2.2 Testing Tools and set-up --> 4.2.4 Statistics and analysis of key indicators

text: 5 Notification API IOT
trace: 5 Notification API IOT

text: 5.1 General
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text: The main objective is to test the interoperability of different vendors' O-CU/O-DU with O-Cloud using notificationrelated APIs. This includes both push and pull modes for event notifications.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text: As stated in Section 4.1, the SUT \(System Under Test\) for the Notification IOT test includes components such as O-Cloud and O-CU/O-DU/SMO.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text: Each IOT test case offers a test purpose, test entrance criteria, initialization conditions, test procedure, and expected results.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text: The main test scenarios covered are as follows:
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text:
* 1\) Functional test of O-Cloud and O-CU/O-DU using notification subscription, query, deletion and event notification API.  
  * 2\) Functional test of O-Cloud and O-CU/O-DU using notification pull API.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.1 General

text: 5.2 Test Configuration
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2 Test Configuration

text: 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements

text: As shown in 5.2-1, the System Under Test \(SUT\) for the O-Cloud Notification IOT test consists of individual O-CU or O-DU components, along with the O-Cloud, which provides the notification framework. The notification framework includes an API producer; O-CU/O-DU act as consumers. O-Cloud, serving as an event generator, provides APIs to
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements
5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements
5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements
5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements
5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements

text: consumers for utilizing these events. These APIs can be used for subscribing to events, unsubscribing, querying subscriptions, and communicating with consumers using pull/push modes.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements

text: At least one O-CU/O-DU and one O-Cloud is required for this test. O-CU/O-DU and O-Cloud are connected through network, and O-CU/O-DU is configured with the endpoint of notification API for the communication.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements

text: Additionally, O-Cloud may need to support traffic mirroring for Protocol Analyzer to capture the requests and responses for analysing.
trace: 5 Notification API IOT --> 5.2.1 System Under Test requirements

text: 7.3.1 General
trace: 7 O2 Interface IOT --> 7.3 O2 IMS Test --> 7.3.1 General

text: The main objective of these O2IMS IOT tests is to validate the interoperability of IMS and FOCOM\(SMO\) over the O2 interface involving the use cases in ORAN WG6.ORCH-USE-CASES, clause 3 \[12\]. This can include orchestration use cases which have completed the Stage 3 specifications for O2IMS in ORAN WG6.TS.O2IMS-INTERFACE \[9\]. Some examples include fault use cases such as alarm subscription, notification or performance use cases such as performance management job creation in compliance with ORAN WG6.TS.O2IMS-INTERFACE \[9\] and O-Cloud Interface Conformance Test Specification ORAN WG6.TS.O-CLOUD-INTF-CONF \[13\].
